title: Bermaz Auto stops distributing XPeng vehicles in Malaysia
text:
Bermaz Auto stops distributing XPeng vehicles in Malaysia Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 16): Bermaz Auto Bhd (KL: BAUTO ) said it will no longer distribute XPeng vehicles in Malaysia as the Chinese electric vehicle (EV) maker has decided to reorganise its local distribution network.
 Its 85%-owned subsidiary, Bermaz Xpeng Sdn Bhd (BXpeng) has ceased XPeng operations with immediate effect, Bermaz Auto said in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Monday.
 BXpeng inked distributorship and warranty claim agreements with subsidiaries of XPeng Inc in March 2024, covering the distribution of XPeng vehicles, after-sales services and spare parts in Malaysia. They were due to expire in March 2027.
 But Bermaz Auto said both parties are now finalising the termination of the agreements and other ancillary arrangements, and an announcement will be made once the separation agreement is signed.
 "During this period, BXpeng will continue to work with the parties concerned to ensure a smooth transition," it said.
 The cessation of BXpeng as XPeng's Malaysian distributor is not expected to have any material financial or operational impact on the Bermaz group for the current financial year, it added.
 Bermaz Auto's separation from XPeng comes about a year after it parted ways with Kia following the South Korean automaker's decision to take over local distribution.
 Meanwhile, the group continues to distribute Mazda vehicles in Malaysia.
 For the first quarter ended July 31, 2026 (1QFY2027), Bermaz Auto's net profit jumped nearly fivefold to RM40.51 million from RM8.28 million a year earlier, driven by higher contributions from associate companies and stronger Mazda sales.
 Revenue for 1QFY2027 rose 12.58% to RM553.08 million from RM491.28 million, mainly on higher sales volumes, particularly the Mazda 3.
 However, profitability from its XPeng operations during the quarter was lower due to increased promotional activities.
 Shares of Bermaz Auto fell two sen or 2.35% to close at 83 sen on Monday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM972.91 million.
